findings.title: Second `self.downsize` replaces the 4-argument one and breaks ResizeEmoji
findings.body: Ruby has no method overloading, so the `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at line 145. The new method takes 3–4 arguments. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5, so it raises `ArgumentError` and custom emoji are no longer downsized to 100x100. Lines 145–147 are now dead code. The fix is to give the dimensions-string variant its own name (e.g. `downsize_to(from, to, dimensions, opts)`), or have the controller call `optimize("downsize", ...)` directly, and keep the width/height signature.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10 MB client limit ignores both size settings, including for attachments
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now checks every type against `10 * 1024` KB instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. The server only downsizes images (uploads_controller.rb:64 requires `FileHelper.is_image?`). For attachments, `UploadValidator#maximum_file_size` (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:80-88) still enforces `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 3072, config/site_settings.yml:516-518). So a 3–10 MB attachment now passes the client check, uploads in full, and only then gets rejected. The reverse happens too: a site that set `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10240 now has valid uploads refused in the browser. Keep `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for attachments. For images, use the larger of the setting and the new downsizing ceiling, and get that ceiling from one place shared with the server instead of literals repeated at lines 182, 246 and uploads_controller.rb:55.

findings.title: Existing QUnit test now fails and no test covers the new behaviour
findings.body: test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61 sets `max_image_size_kb = 5`, uploads a 10 KB image and asserts it is rejected with `max_size_kb: 5`. With the hard-coded 10 MB limit, `validUpload` returns true and the alert is never shown, so this test fails. The PR also adds no spec for the server-side downsizing loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-70.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and flattens or fails on animated GIFs
findings.body: The loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s return value. If `convert_with` fails (optimized_image.rb:160-169), the same command reruns on the same large file up to 5 times before the validator rejects it. When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the tempfile path ends in `.gif`, `optimize` uses the gifsicle path (optimized_image.rb:155, 137-138, 120): `--resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle expects WxH geometry there, so this likely fails on every attempt. When the setting is off, `convert #{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb:129) keeps only the first frame, so a large animated GIF is silently stored as a still image. Stop the loop when `downsize` returns false. Consider skipping GIFs, or deriving a WxH geometry from the image's current size.

findings.title: Could truncated API URL downloads now get re-encoded into corrupt images?
findings.body: `FileHelper.download` stops reading once the file exceeds `max_file_size` and returns the partial file anyway (lib/file_helper.rb:16-25). Before this change the cap was `max_image_size_kb`, so a truncated file was always over the limit and the validator rejected it. Now the cap is 10 MB. With the default 3072 KB setting, a remote image over 10 MB is cut at about 10.5 MB, and the new loop then runs `convert` on that partial image until it fits. Does `convert` exit 0 on a truncated JPEG/PNG? If it does, the API stores a visibly corrupt image with no error. Separately, sites with `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 can no longer import images that large by URL.

summary:
Don't merge this as is: one change breaks custom emoji resizing. `OptimizedImage` now defines `self.downsize` twice (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:145` and `:149`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (`app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14`), which passes 5 arguments, raises `ArgumentError` and emoji are no longer shrunk to 100x100.

The PR description ("automatically downsize large images") matches the server loop in `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70`. It leaves out two side effects of the hard-coded 10 MB limits:

- **Browser size check now ignores the settings** (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182`). It applies 10 MB to attachments too, and attachments are never downsized. So files between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10 MB upload in full and are then rejected by the server. Sites with limits set above 10 MB now have valid uploads refused in the browser.
- **Existing test breaks**: the QUnit test at `test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61` will fail. The new server-side loop has no tests.

Smaller points:

- **The loop never checks whether a resize worked.** A failed `convert` is retried up to 5 times on the same file. Animated GIFs either fail every time (gifsicle likely doesn't accept `80%`) or are silently flattened to their first frame.
- **Open question on API URL uploads**: the download cap is now 10 MB (`uploads_controller.rb:55`), and the download helper returns the partial file when it stops early. I couldn't confirm whether `convert` succeeds on a truncated image; if it does, the API stores a corrupt image with no error.
